title: MutatingWebhook cert rotation blocks Helm CRD upgrade path for on-prem clusters
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
Several on-prem / VPC customers reported failed Helm upgrades when the operator chart attempted a CRD migration that triggers cert rotation for the mutatingwebhook. The operator pod entered crashloop/reconcile stalls, admission errors were recorded across control-plane logs, and rollout was blocked for affected clusters.

Scope / Affected customers:
- Initial reports from two mid-market customers (CUST-A, CUST-B) upgrading from operator v1.7.x -> 1.8.0.
- Later confirmed by internal test clusters with custom mutatingwebhookconfigurations and clusters that have disabled the default CSR signer.

Primary observed symptoms:
- Helm upgrade failed at the post-upgrade hook stage with timeout waiting for CRD migration.
- Operator logs showed repeated failures: "webhook TLS cert mismatch" and "failed to create ValidatingWebhookConfiguration: admission webhook timed out".
- Kube API returned 403/500 on admission requests for operator-managed resources, causing controllers to stall.
- Some customer patch releases reverted operator image leading to cluster drift.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-09 09:12: First customer ticket opened with upgrade failure and operator crashloop.
- 2026-03-09 12:30: Engineering triage; reproduced failure in multi-zone test cluster.
- 2026-03-10 03:40: Root cause hypothesis: cert rotation path creates new cert but webhookconfiguration update races with kube-apiserver and some clusters reject the new cert due to older CA bundles or custom webhook namespaces.
- 2026-03-11 10:20: Hotfix branch created; initial patch adds explicit certificate reconciliation + pre-upgrade hook to snapshot webhook config.
- 2026-03-12 18:00: Patch validated in CI + internal staging; created release candidate onprem-2026.03.1-rc1.
- 2026-03-14 08:45: Hotfix rollout started to impacted customers using paid hotfix channel.

Root cause (detailed):
- The operator's CRD migration introduced an automated mutatingwebhook certificate rotation. The rotation logic attempted an in-place update of the MutatingWebhookConfiguration and the TLS secret but did not block or version-check the existing apiserver CA bundle. On clusters where the CSR signer is non-standard or where operators had custom webhook entries (different names/namespace), the apiserver rejected the new webhook config or accepted it but failed subsequent TLS handshakes.
- There is a race between (a) creation of the new TLS secret, (b) update of the webhook resource, and (c) in-flight admission requests routed to old webhook endpoints. That race leads to transient admission failures which broke controller reconciliation and Helm's upgrade hooks.
- Config drift: several customers had manually-modified MutatingWebhookConfiguration entries (extra conversions, different timeout/severity fields) that drifted from the operator's expected values; the upgrade path assumed a declarative overwrite which caused merge conflicts and API rejections.

Mitigations / Temporary workarounds provided to customers:
- For immediate unblock: revert operator to v1.7.x using helm rollback and mark webhook TLS secret immutable until hotfix applied. (Provided rollback commands and watch scripts.)
- For clusters where rollback not possible: manually patch the MutatingWebhookConfiguration to include the old CA bundle and allow operator to rotate certificates in two-step: create new secret, then update webhook config during a low-traffic window.
- Where manual intervention would be risky, we offered to perform concierge upgrades under support SLA.

Hotfix and engineering resolution steps:
- Implemented certificate reconciliation loop that:
  1) verifies the new TLS secret's CA bundle matches apiserver expectations before switching the webhook configuration,
  2) applies a lightweight lock (annotation) on MutatingWebhookConfiguration to prevent concurrent updates from other controllers, and
  3) adds a pre-upgrade helm hook to create a backup copy of the existing webhook configuration (mutating + validating) and TLS secrets.
- Helm chart change: added pre-upgrade hook job and increased timeout for post-install when CRD migrations are present.
- Added e2e tests that simulate disabled CSR signer and manual webhook modifications.
- Release: onprem-2026.03.1 (hotfix) with operator image tag operator:v1.8.0-hotfix.1.

Verification performed:
- Smoke test matrix against k8s 1.24, 1.25 with default and custom webhook configs.
- Regression run for Helm upgrades across sample customer manifests.
- Observability: added Prometheus alert to detect >5% admission failures for >5m during upgrade windows.

Rollout plan:
- 2026-03-14: hotfix release made available via dedicated channel and helm repo - applied to most at-risk on-prem clusters under concierge.
- 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-20: follow-up automated rollout for remaining dedicated/private customers with scheduled maintenance windows.

Communication and customer-facing artifacts:
- Sent targeted incident emails to affected customers with rollback instructions and hotfix schedule.
- Confluence runbook created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/ENG-14807+MutatingWebhook+Hotfix
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/2845 (cert reconciliation), https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/512 (helm hook + chart changes).
- Internal dashboard for upgrade failures: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/upgrade-failures/helm-upgrades

Open follow-ups / postmortem actions:
- (P0) Add pre-merge static analysis for webhook modifications to detect potential drift with cluster-customized webhook configs.
- (P1) Create an operator-mode "safe-rotate" that performs two-phase cert handover for all cluster types.
- (P2) Add explicit guardrail docs for customers explaining manual webhook customizations and how to prepare for major operator upgrades.
- (P2) Product: consider exposing a helm upgrade flag --safe-webhook-rotate to force out-of-band rotation.

Acceptance criteria for closing this ticket:
- Hotfix release deployed to all impacted customers and no new upgrade failures reported for 72h after rollout.
- Post-deployment e2e tests pass in CI for the upgrade matrix.
- Runbook reviewed by SRE and Security and stored in Confluence.
